Title: User Manager signs in and reaches the User management workspace
Preconditions: Tenant provisioned at WEB_APP_URL. A User Manager account exists with a completed first login.
Steps: 1) Open WEB_APP_URL; 2) Enter the User Manager email and permanent password; 3) Click Sign in; 4) Wait for the authenticated shell
Expected Result: The authenticated shell renders with the User management module available and no first-login prompt.
Notes: Case USM-01 of docs/testcases/07-user-manager.md, implemented through signInRole(user_manager) in tests/web/testcases/user-manager.spec.ts.

Title: Sidebar exposes User management only and no foreign role module
Preconditions: User Manager signed in on the tenant URL.
Steps: 1) Read the Primary navigation region; 2) Assert User management is present; 3) Assert Access governance, Exam configuration, Evaluation desk, Digitization, Chief master and Allocation engine are absent
Expected Result: Only User management is rendered in the sidebar and every other role workspace is absent.
Notes: The spec asserts User management plus three absent foreign modules. Mirrors the section 19 role matrix.

Title: Identity endpoint reports the User Manager role
Preconditions: User Manager session cookie available.
Steps: 1) Sign in as the User Manager; 2) GET /api/v1/auth/me; 3) Read the role field
Expected Result: The response reports role = user_manager so downstream scope checks are evaluated for the right role.
Notes: The spec asserts role = user_manager through AUTH_ME.

Title: Sign out revokes access to the user management API
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with a readable security catalog.
Steps: 1) Click the Sign out control; 2) Confirm the login page is shown; 3) GET /api/v1/security/catalog with the old cookies
Expected Result: The session ends and the security catalog is no longer readable after sign out.
Notes: Confirms the section 5 logout contract for this role. LoginPage and shell locators already exist.

Title: Workspace survives a page reload
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with User management open.
Steps: 1) Reload the browser page; 2) Assert the shell heading and Primary navigation; 3) Assert User management is still available
Expected Result: The session persists across the reload and the User management workspace is unchanged.
Notes: Same reload contract already asserted for the shell in the first-login spec.

Title: Shell banner controls are available to the User Manager
Preconditions: User Manager signed in.
Steps: 1) Sign in as the User Manager; 2) Read the shell banner region; 3) Assert Select language, Notifications, Account settings and Sign out are visible
Expected Result: All shell banner controls are present for the User Manager, so session and locale actions stay reachable.
Test Data: AuthenticatedShellPage locators: Select language, Notifications, Account settings, Sign out
Notes: Locators verified in pages/AuthenticatedShellPage.ts.

Title: User management workspace exposes the Add user action
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with the User management module available.
Steps: 1) Open User management; 2) Locate the Add user action; 3) Assert it is enabled
Expected Result: The Add user action is present and enabled, so provisioning can start from the workspace.
Test Data: Add user, captured in prompts/KTR_WEB_TEST_PROMPTS.md section 14
Notes: No page object exists for User management yet. Confirm the accessible role and name of Add user before automating.

Title: Add university user form exposes the documented fields
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with a valid step-up and the Add university user form open.
Steps: 1) Read every field on the form; 2) Assert first name, last name, email, Role, Operational centre and Module access are present; 3) Assert the Create user action is present
Expected Result: The form exposes exactly the documented provisioning fields plus the centre picker and module access list.
Notes: Field labels were captured in the prompts but not in a page object. Record real labels and name attributes before writing locators.

Title: Security context endpoint reports the acting User Manager
Preconditions: User Manager session cookie available.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/auth/security-context; 2) Read the reported identity and step-up state
Expected Result: The response identifies the User Manager account and its current step-up state, matching the session in use.
Notes: Response shape for this role was not captured. Assert identity fields only after reading a live response.

Title: Security catalog is readable by the User Manager with members, centres and role rules
Preconditions: User Manager session cookie available. Tenant has at least one active centre and one member.
Steps: 1) Sign in as the User Manager; 2) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 3) Inspect the top-level keys
Expected Result: A 200 response carrying members, centres, role_module_rules, module_catalog and policy.
Notes: The schema lists every required key. The unauthenticated counterpart expects 401.

Title: Membership creation without a step-up is refused
Preconditions: User Manager session established without a prior step-up in the current window.
Steps: 1) Sign in as the User Manager; 2) POST /api/v1/security/memberships with a valid scanner payload; 3) Read the status code and re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The create is refused with 401, 403 or 428 and no new member appears in the catalog.
Test Data: role scanner_operator, enabled_modules [digitization], operational_centre_id of an active centre
Notes: The spec expects 401, 403 or 428 for the same payload.

Title: Step-up with the User Manager own password succeeds
Preconditions: User Manager session established.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/auth/step-up with the User Manager own password; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: Step-up returns 200 so the sensitive create action is permitted inside the validity window.
Test Data: Routes.AUTH_STEP_UP with the acting account password
Notes: The create flow depends on this: the spec asserts step-up returns 200 before creating.

Title: Step-up with a wrong password is refused
Preconditions: User Manager session established. Candidate user data prepared.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/auth/step-up with an incorrect password; 2) Attempt the membership create; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: Step-up fails, the create is refused and no member is created.
Test Data: step-up body: password set to a deliberately wrong value
Notes: The refusal status for a bad step-up was not captured. Record the status code before asserting it.

Title: Crafted create payload cannot self-declare a completed step-up
Preconditions: User Manager session without a step-up in the current window.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/security/memberships with step_up true, step_up_verified true and mfa_verified true added to the body; 2) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The create is still refused and no member is created, because step-up is proven server-side per session.
Test Data: extra body keys: step_up, step_up_verified, mfa_verified
Notes: Backend field names for the step-up proof are not documented. Confirm which keys the API ignores.

Title: A second create inside the step-up window does not re-prompt
Preconditions: Successful step-up inside policy.step_up_minutes. One membership already created in this window.
Steps: 1) Read policy.step_up_minutes from the catalog; 2) Create a second user without a new step-up; 3) Read the status code
Expected Result: The second create succeeds without a new step-up while the window is still valid, so bulk onboarding stays usable.
Notes: Window reuse is implied by the step_up_minutes policy field but was not captured end to end.

Title: Step-up is required again after the validity window elapses
Preconditions: Successful step-up and policy.step_up_minutes read from the catalog.
Steps: 1) Perform a stepped-up create; 2) Wait past step_up_minutes; 3) Repeat the create without a new step-up
Expected Result: The second create is refused with 401, 403 or 428 until the User Manager re-authenticates.
Notes: Requires a live wait or an Admin policy change. Do not shorten the policy on a shared tenant without approval.

Title: Authenticator-code step-up completes for an authenticator-enabled account
Preconditions: User Manager account with authenticator_enabled true in the catalog.
Steps: 1) Open the sensitive-action dialog; 2) Choose Authenticator code; 3) Enter a valid code and click Verify
Expected Result: Step-up completes through the authenticator path and the create action is permitted.
Notes: The Password or Authenticator code then Verify path is captured in sections 10, 14 and 18. Never store the code.

Title: Wrong authenticator code is refused
Preconditions: User Manager account with authenticator_enabled true.
Steps: 1) Open the sensitive-action dialog; 2) Choose Authenticator code; 3) Enter an invalid code and click Verify
Expected Result: The dialog reports the failure, stays open and no membership is created.
Notes: Message copy was not captured. Assert refusal and no created member, not a specific string.

Title: Step-up cannot be borrowed from another account
Preconditions: Two valid accounts: the User Manager and any other role account with a known password.
Steps: 1) Repeat a create in a User Manager session that has no step-up, supplying the other account password to /api/v1/auth/step-up; 2) Read the status code; 3) Attempt the create
Expected Result: The foreign password is rejected for the User Manager session and the create stays refused.
Test Data: other role credentials from the run secret store
Notes: Step-up is documented as re-verifying the acting account. Confirm the API rejects a foreign credential.

Title: Scanner operator is created with an active centre and a handover
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with a valid step-up. At least one active centre exists.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/security/memberships with the scanner payload; 2) Read the status code and body
Expected Result: The membership is created and the response carries a handover with the intended role and a temporary password.
Test Data: first_name first, last_name scanner, role scanner_operator, enabled_modules [digitization], operational_centre_id of the first active centre
Notes: Writes stay gated behind DVS_ALLOW_WRITES=true, as in the spec.

Title: Handover reports the role, the module list and a temporary password
Preconditions: A scanner operator was just created by the User Manager.
Steps: 1) Read the handover returned by the scanner create; 2) Read role and enabled_modules; 3) Read temporary_password
Expected Result: role = scanner_operator, enabled_modules = [digitization] and temporary_password is non-empty.
Test Data: same payload as the scanner create case
Notes: The spec asserts exactly these three fields on the handover.

Title: Handover carries an expiry for the temporary password
Preconditions: A scanner operator was just created by the User Manager.
Steps: 1) Read expires_at from the handover body; 2) Compare it with the current time
Expected Result: expires_at is a valid future timestamp, so the handover credential is time-boxed.
Notes: expires_at is a required schema field but its lifetime was not captured. Record the observed lifetime.

Title: Handover sheet renders User ID, Temporary password, Expires and Done
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with a valid step-up. One user created from the UI.
Steps: 1) Create a scanner operator from Add university user; 2) Read the handover sheet fields; 3) Click Done
Expected Result: The handover sheet shows User ID, Temporary password, Expires and Done for the new user.
Notes: Shown once per user, so the case needs a fresh user per run. Never store or screenshot the credential.

Title: Handover Done dismisses the sheet and the member row remains
Preconditions: A handover sheet is open for a user just created from the UI.
Steps: 1) Click Done; 2) Read the member list; 3) Reload and re-read the list
Expected Result: The sheet closes, the new member row remains with its role and centre, and no credential detail stays on screen.
Test Data: the user created immediately before this case
Notes: Confirms the sheet is the only credential surface and dismissal does not roll back the create.

Title: Provisioned scanner completes first login and reaches Digitization
Preconditions: A scanner operator provisioned with an active centre and a temporary password in the run secret store.
Steps: 1) Sign in with the temporary password; 2) Set the permanent password; 3) Assert the Digitization module is available; 4) GET /api/v1/auth/me
Expected Result: The scanner reaches the Digitization workspace and the identity endpoint reports scanner_operator.
Notes: The spec covers this outcome end to end, including the scanner reaching the receiving catalog.

Title: Newly provisioned user appears in the security catalog
Preconditions: A provisioned scanner operator completed the first login.
Steps: 1) Re-read /api/v1/security/catalog as the User Manager; 2) Search members for the new email
Expected Result: The member is present with the intended role and centre.
Test Data: new user email with a run-unique suffix
Notes: The spec asserts the same catalog refresh.

Title: Catalog member row reports onboarding status and active flag
Preconditions: A member was just created and has not yet onboarded.
Steps: 1) Read the member row from the catalog; 2) Inspect onboarding_status and is_active
Expected Result: onboarding_status reflects the pending first login and is_active is true for a usable account.
Notes: Field names are verified in the schema. Allowed onboarding_status values were not captured.

Title: Member row reports a pending temporary password before first login
Preconditions: A user was created and has not signed in yet.
Steps: 1) Read the member row before the first login; 2) Inspect has_temporary_password
Expected Result: has_temporary_password is true, matching the issued handover.
Notes: Field is required in the schema, but the value transition was not captured in traffic.

Title: Member row clears the temporary-password flag after first login
Preconditions: The same member completed the first login and set a permanent password.
Steps: 1) Re-read the catalog after the permanent password is set; 2) Inspect has_temporary_password and onboarding_status
Expected Result: has_temporary_password is false and onboarding_status no longer reports a pending handover.
Notes: Confirms the single-use handover is reflected in audit-facing catalog state.

Title: Created scanner is bound to exactly the selected operational centre
Preconditions: Active centre id resolved from the catalog.
Steps: 1) Create the scanner operator with operational_centre_id; 2) Read operational_centre_id from the handover and from the catalog row
Expected Result: Both values equal the selected centre id and no other centre is attached.
Test Data: operational_centre_id of the first active centre
Notes: operational_centre_id is a required schema field and the spec passes the same id on create.

Title: Users created for two different active centres keep their own centre
Preconditions: Two active centres exist. User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a scanner operator for centre A; 2) Create a scanner operator for centre B; 3) Read operational_centre_id from both handovers and catalog rows
Expected Result: Each member is bound to its own centre with no cross-assignment.
Test Data: centre ids A and B from the catalog, two run-unique emails
Notes: Extends the single-centre check to the multi-centre onboarding case.

Title: Created member is listed exactly once across repeated catalog reads
Preconditions: One member created in this run.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog three times; 2) Count rows for the created email in each response
Expected Result: Exactly one row exists for the email in every read, so the list is not duplicating members.
Notes: Guards against list duplication after writes.

Title: Acting User Manager own member row is visible in the catalog
Preconditions: User Manager signed in and its email known.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 2) Search members for the acting User Manager email; 3) Read role and modules
Expected Result: The acting User Manager row is present with role user_manager and the documented module list.
Notes: Self-visibility in the member list is not documented. Record whether the acting account is listed.

Title: A rejected create leaves the catalog unchanged
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up. A rejected create already attempted with a duplicate email.
Steps: 1) Re-read the catalog after the rejected create; 2) Count rows for the rejected email; 3) Read the member count
Expected Result: No member is added and the member count is unchanged by the rejected attempt.
Test Data: duplicate email used in the rejected attempt
Notes: Validation must not leave partial state behind.

Title: Two consecutive creates return distinct member and user ids
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up. Two run-unique emails prepared.
Steps: 1) Create user A; 2) Create user B; 3) Compare id and user_id from both handovers
Expected Result: Both creates return 2xx with different member ids and different user ids.
Test Data: two run-unique emails, same role and centre
Notes: The spec covers repeated provisioning consistency sequentially.

Title: Scanner operator defaults to the digitization module only
Preconditions: Active centre exists. User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Read role_module_rules.scanner_operator from the catalog; 2) Create a scanner operator with the default modules; 3) Read enabled_modules
Expected Result: The created member carries digitization only and no configuration, security or evaluation module.
Notes: Least-privilege check. testdata/dvs_user_provisioning.json lists digitization for scanner_operator.

Title: User Manager role defaults to the enterprise and security modules
Preconditions: An Admin provisioned a second User Manager account.
Steps: 1) Read role_module_rules.user_manager from the catalog; 2) Compare it with the created User Manager enabled_modules
Expected Result: The created User Manager carries enterprise and security only, matching the documented default.
Notes: The default list comes from testdata/dvs_user_provisioning.json. Confirm the tenant value before asserting equality.

Title: Module access selected in the form persists unchanged
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up and a role whose defaults are known.
Steps: 1) Create a user with an explicit enabled_modules list; 2) Read enabled_modules from the handover; 3) Re-read the catalog row
Expected Result: Both the handover and the catalog report exactly the submitted module list, in the same order.
Notes: Guards against silent module rewriting by the server.

Title: Module access list offers digitization only for the scanner operator role
Preconditions: Add university user form open with role Scanner operator selected.
Steps: 1) Read the Module access section; 2) Assert digitization is listed; 3) Assert configuration, security and evaluation are not offered
Expected Result: The module picker cannot grant a module outside the scanner operator role default.
Notes: Section 14 requires reviewing Module access for the role. Confirm whether the list is read-only or selectable.

Title: Role selector does not offer Examination controller
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with the Add university user form open.
Steps: 1) Open the Role selector; 2) Read every option; 3) Assert Examination controller is absent
Expected Result: Examination controller is not offerable, matching the current build where the role is legacy only.
Test Data: section 10 role note: Examination controller is not a provisionable role
Notes: Assert the absence, never the landing page of that legacy role. Confirm the option list on the tenant.

Title: Role selector offers Exam invigilator as an optional role
Preconditions: User Manager signed in with the Add university user form open.
Steps: 1) Open the Role selector; 2) Assert Exam invigilator is listed; 3) Read the module access it prefills
Expected Result: Exam invigilator is selectable and its prefilled module list matches the tenant role rules.
Notes: testdata/dvs_user_provisioning.json marks this role optional and records that its module list was never captured.

Title: Exam invigilator can be provisioned with a centre and appears in the catalog
Preconditions: An active centre exists. User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create an exam invigilator with the active centre; 2) Read the status code and handover; 3) Re-read the catalog member row
Expected Result: The exam invigilator is created, bound to the chosen centre and listed with the role exam_invigilator.
Test Data: role exam_invigilator, active centre id, run-unique email
Notes: Role is optional and its module defaults are unknown, so assert role and centre only until the module list is captured.

Title: Intended role is persisted and never silently substituted
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a scanner operator; 2) Read role from the handover and from the catalog member row; 3) Confirm the member can open Digitization and not Evaluation desk
Expected Result: The member stays scanner_operator with the digitization module, so a wrong default cannot pass as success.
Notes: Guards the observed anomaly in section 10 where a scanner was first created with role evaluator.

Title: Scanner operator without an operational centre is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/security/memberships with operational_centre_id null; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and no membership is created.
Notes: The spec asserts a 4xx for the same payload.

Title: Duplicate email is rejected and one member row remains
Preconditions: A scanner operator already provisioned with a known email.
Steps: 1) Re-post the same email with valid data; 2) Read the status code; 3) Count catalog rows for that email
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and exactly one member row exists for the email.
Test Data: email of the user created earlier in the run
Notes: The spec asserts a 4xx and one remaining row.

Title: Duplicate email differing only by letter case is rejected
Preconditions: A member exists with the lower-case form of an email.
Steps: 1) Create the same email with upper-case letters; 2) Read the status code; 3) Count catalog rows
Expected Result: The create is rejected and no second identity is created for the same mailbox.
Notes: Case-folding of institutional email is not documented. Confirm the tenant treats the address as case-insensitive.

Title: Duplicate email with surrounding spaces is rejected
Preconditions: A member exists with a known email.
Steps: 1) Create the same email padded with leading and trailing spaces; 2) Read the status code; 3) Count catalog rows
Expected Result: The create is rejected or normalized to the existing identity, and no duplicate member exists.
Test Data: existing email padded with leading and trailing spaces
Notes: Depends on whether the server trims before the uniqueness check. Record the behaviour.

Title: Missing first name is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with first_name empty; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: The spec asserts a 4xx for an empty first name.

Title: Missing last name is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with last_name empty; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: The spec asserts a 4xx for an empty last name.

Title: Whitespace-only first name is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with first_name of three spaces; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The value is rejected as empty, so a member cannot be created with a blank display name.
Notes: Whitespace-only handling was not captured. Confirm the server trims before the required-field check.

Title: Malformed email without an at-sign is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with email not-an-email; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: The spec asserts a 4xx for the same value.

Title: Empty email is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with email as an empty string; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: The status code for an empty email was not captured. Record it.

Title: Email with two at-signs is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with email a@@b.com; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx validation error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: Confirms a server-side format check, not only the browser input type.

Title: Email without a domain is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with email user@; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx validation error is returned and nothing is created.
Notes: Same family as the malformed email case with a different shape.

Title: Email containing an internal space is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with email first last@example.com; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx validation error is returned and nothing is created.
Test Data: email with an internal space before the at-sign
Notes: Copy-paste from a spreadsheet is the realistic source of this input.

Title: Email local part accepts 64 characters and rejects 65
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a user whose local part is 64 characters; 2) Repeat with 65 characters; 3) Compare the status codes
Expected Result: The 64-character local part is accepted and the 65-character one is rejected with a 4xx error.
Test Data: 64 and 65 character local parts at example.com
Notes: The RFC upper bound is assumed. Confirm the server limit before asserting the boundary.

Title: Full email length boundary is enforced at 254 characters
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a user with a 254-character email; 2) Repeat with 255 characters; 3) Compare the status codes
Expected Result: The 254-character email is accepted and the 255-character one is rejected with a 4xx error.
Notes: Bound from RFC 5321. Confirm the server limit, do not assume it.

Title: Maximum-length first name is accepted and one over is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a user with the longest allowed first name; 2) Repeat with one extra character; 3) Compare the status codes
Expected Result: The maximum-length name is stored intact and the over-length value is rejected with a 4xx error.
Test Data: first_name lengths at and above the documented maximum
Notes: The column limit is not documented. Record the first rejected length.

Title: Unicode names are stored intact
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a user with a Kannada first name and a Devanagari last name; 2) Read the name from the handover and the catalog row
Expected Result: The stored name matches the submitted Unicode text without transliteration or truncation.
Test Data: first_name in Kannada script, last_name in Devanagari script
Notes: Localisation of the member table is not documented. Confirm both rendering and storage.

Title: Missing role is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with the role key removed; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and no member is created without a role.
Test Data: payload with the role key removed
Notes: Section 10 lists missing role as a negative case but the API status was not captured.

Title: Empty role string is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with role as an empty string; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and no member is created with a blank role.
Notes: Guards a client-side bypass of the required role selector.

Title: Unrecognised role value is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with role scanner, an alias rather than a role key; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and no member is created with an unknown role.
Notes: Section 10 lists missing role but not alias handling. Record the response.

Title: Unknown operational centre id is rejected
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST a scanner operator with a random UUID as operational_centre_id; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: A 4xx error is returned and no member is bound to an unknown centre.
Notes: Confirms the centre is validated server-side, not only by the picker.

Title: Centre that is not activated cannot be selected
Preconditions: An Admin created a centre that passed readiness but was never activated.
Steps: 1) Open the operational centre picker in Add university user; 2) Search for the inactive centre; 3) Attempt to select it
Expected Result: The inactive centre is not selectable, so provisioning cannot target a centre that is not live.
Test Data: centre with a status other than active from the catalog
Notes: Section 9 requires Check readiness then Activate before a centre is assignable. Confirm picker filtering.

Title: No operational centre option creates a user without a centre
Preconditions: Add university user form open. Active centre exists.
Steps: 1) Choose No operational centre; 2) Fill the remaining fields for a non-scanner role; 3) Submit and re-read the catalog row
Expected Result: The member is created without a centre and reports operational_centre_id null, so a centre is not silently attached.
Notes: Section 10 documents the No operational centre option. Confirm which roles accept it.

Title: Scanner created without modules cannot reach Digitization
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create a scanner operator with enabled_modules empty; 2) Complete the first login; 3) Read the sidebar and GET /api/v1/scanning/catalog
Expected Result: The user is created but Digitization is not exposed and the scanning catalog is refused, so an empty module list cannot grant access by default.
Notes: Server behaviour for an empty module list was not captured. If the create is refused instead, record that.

Title: Unknown payload keys are ignored and not applied
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST a valid scanner payload plus unknown keys such as department and employee_code; 2) Re-read the catalog member row
Expected Result: The create succeeds as a normal scanner operator and the unknown keys are absent from role, permissions and modules.
Notes: custom_fields is an open object in the schema, so verify where unknown keys land.

Title: Second membership for an existing identity is handled explicitly
Preconditions: An identity already exists in the tenant with a member row.
Steps: 1) Create a membership for the same email under a different role; 2) Read the status code and existing_identity
Expected Result: The response is either explicit existing_identity handling or a 4xx error, and never a silent duplicate row.
Test Data: existing member email with role exam_invigilator
Notes: existing_identity is a required handover field, so the server models this case. Capture the actual outcome.

Title: Over-long first name fails without a server error
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with a 1000-character first name; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: A 4xx validation error is returned, never a 5xx, so malformed input cannot destabilise the service.
Notes: Checks that the boundary degrades into validation rather than a server error.

Title: First login shows the Set your password screen with the requirements list
Preconditions: A user was just provisioned and has not signed in.
Steps: 1) Open WEB_APP_URL; 2) Sign in with the temporary password; 3) Read the screen
Expected Result: The Set your password screen appears with New password, Confirm password and the password requirements list, and the shell is not yet rendered.
Test Data: temporary password from the handover, used once
Notes: SetPasswordPage locators are verified. Temporary passwords stay in the run secret store only.

Title: Password confirmation mismatch is rejected
Preconditions: Set your password screen open for a provisioned user.
Steps: 1) Enter a valid new password; 2) Enter a different confirmation; 3) Click Set password and continue
Expected Result: The screen reports the mismatch, stays open and the temporary password remains the only credential.
Test Data: new password plus a one-character-different confirmation
Notes: Section 3 negative variant. SetPasswordPage.setPassword already accepts a separate confirmation.

Title: Password shorter than twelve characters is rejected
Preconditions: Set your password screen open for a provisioned user.

Expected Result: The 11-character password is rejected with the requirements hint and the compliant password is accepted.

Title: Password with repeated or sequential characters is rejected
Preconditions: Set your password screen open for a provisioned user.

Expected Result: The password is rejected because it breaks the no continuous sequence or repeating characters rule.

Title: Temporary password stops working after the permanent password is set

Title: Expired temporary password is refused

Title: Temporary password grants only the set-password screen
Preconditions: A provisioned user has not completed the first login.

Expected Result: No role module is reachable and the protected catalog call is refused until the permanent password is set.
Test Data: temporary password from a fresh handover
Notes: Pre-password session scope is not documented. Confirm the server refuses module access mid-onboarding.

Title: Permanent password lands the provisioned user in the intended role shell
Preconditions: A provisioned user is on the Set your password screen.
Steps: 1) Set a compliant permanent password; 2) Assert the shell heading and Primary navigation; 3) GET /api/v1/auth/me
Expected Result: The user reaches the shell for the provisioned role and the identity endpoint reports that role.
Notes: Closes the handover loop started by the scanner create case.

Title: User Manager cannot create a university administrator

Title: User Manager cannot create a Chairman
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.

Title: User Manager cannot create an Evaluator through memberships
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.

Expected Result: The create is refused as out of scope, because evaluators are provisioned through evaluator management and nomination.
Notes: testdata notes evaluator and chief are created through evaluator-management, not memberships. Confirm the refusal.

Title: User Manager cannot create a member with role admin
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with role admin; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The create is refused with a 4xx error and no tenant administrator is created.

Title: User Manager cannot save the security policy
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up and a readable catalog policy object.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 2) PUT /api/v1/security/policy with the policy object; 3) Read the status code
Expected Result: The save is refused with 401, 403 or 428 and the policy version is unchanged.
Test Data: policy object read from the catalog
Notes: The spec asserts a refusal on the policy save.

Title: User Manager cannot read the exam configuration catalog
Preconditions: User Manager signed in.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/configuration/catalog; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: The read is refused with 401 or 403 and no academic configuration data is returned.
Notes: The spec asserts 401 or 403 for the same route.

Title: User Manager cannot read the scanning and receiving catalogs
Preconditions: User Manager signed in.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/scanning/catalog; 2) GET /api/v1/receiving/guided/catalog; 3) Read both status codes
Expected Result: Both reads are refused, because the User Manager has no digitization module.
Notes: Refusal status per route was not captured for this role. Record both codes.

Title: User Manager cannot read the marking workspace
Preconditions: User Manager signed in and a known assignment id available from the run.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/marking/assignments/{assignmentId}/workspace; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: The read is refused with 401 or 403 and no script content is returned.
Notes: Requires an assignment created by the Chief. Assert the refusal, never script content.

Title: User Manager cannot create an operational centre
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/phase4/centres with a centre payload; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog centres list
Expected Result: The create is refused and the centres list is unchanged, because centre operations are an Admin action.
Test Data: centre name ADMIEZO, no generated code supplied
Notes: Section 9 places centre creation in Admin Access governance. Confirm the User Manager refusal.

Title: Direct navigation does not unlock an Admin module for the User Manager
Preconditions: User Manager signed in.
Steps: 1) Navigate directly to the tenant root and to a deep link used by the Admin Access governance module; 2) Read the rendered modules; 3) Assert Access governance is absent
Expected Result: The Admin module does not render and the sidebar remains limited to User management.
Test Data: tenant root URL plus an Admin module deep link
Notes: The app is a single-page app and stays on the tenant root. Record the deep link that is actually rejected.

Title: Catalog reports no policy-management capability for the User Manager
Preconditions: User Manager signed in.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 2) Read capabilities.manage_security_policy and capabilities.manage_users
Expected Result: manage_security_policy is false while manage_users is true, matching least privilege for the role.
Notes: Capability values for this role were not captured. Record them before asserting.

Title: User Manager cannot see another centre users in the catalog
Preconditions: Two active centres exist with members in both. The User Manager is scoped to one centre.
Steps: 1) Read the catalog as the User Manager; 2) Filter members by the foreign centre; 3) Compare with the Admin view
Expected Result: Members of the foreign centre are absent from the User Manager view and no foreign email is disclosed.
Test Data: two active centres with at least one member each
Notes: The spec asserts that foreign centre users are absent.

Title: Wildcard permissions cannot be granted by the client
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST a scanner membership with permissions set to a wildcard entry; 2) Read permissions from the handover; 3) Re-read the catalog member row
Expected Result: The stored permissions do not contain the wildcard and the member gains no policy or configuration rights.
Test Data: permissions with a single asterisk entry
Notes: permissions is a free array in the schema, so the server must filter it. Record what is stored.

Title: Custom fields cannot overwrite role or active state
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST with custom_fields carrying role university_admin and is_active true; 2) Re-read the catalog member row
Expected Result: The member keeps the submitted role and custom_fields never overrides role, is_active or permissions.
Test Data: custom_fields containing role and is_active keys
Notes: custom_fields is an open object. Confirm the server ignores reserved keys inside it.

Title: Modules beyond the role default are refused or dropped
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) POST a scanner membership with enabled_modules containing digitization plus configuration and security; 2) Read enabled_modules from the handover and the catalog
Expected Result: Only digitization is retained, so a crafted payload cannot widen the new user module scope.
Notes: The default-module case asserts least privilege on create. This case asserts the server filters an inflated list.

Title: Foreign operational centre id is refused for a scanner create
Preconditions: Two centres exist and the User Manager is scoped to one.
Steps: 1) POST a scanner membership with the foreign centre id; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The create is refused and no member is bound to the foreign centre.
Notes: Centre scope must be enforced server-side, not by the picker. Record the refusal code.

Title: Create without the CSRF header is refused
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up but no X-CSRFToken header on the request.
Steps: 1) POST /api/v1/security/memberships without X-CSRFToken; 2) Read the status code; 3) Re-read the catalog
Expected Result: The request is refused with a 4xx CSRF error and nothing is created.
Notes: utils/apiClient.ts sends X-CSRFToken and Origin on writes, so the backend enforces CSRF. Confirm the status code.

Title: Create from a foreign Origin is refused
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up and a CSRF token.
Steps: 1) POST the membership with a foreign Origin header; 2) Read the status code
Expected Result: The request is refused, so a cross-site page cannot drive provisioning with a stolen session.
Notes: Origin checking is implied by the extraHTTPHeaders contract in utils/apiClient.ts. Record the status code.

Title: Catalog reads never expose temporary passwords
Preconditions: At least one member holds a pending handover.
Steps: 1) GET /api/v1/security/catalog; 2) Search the raw response text for the handover credential
Expected Result: The catalog contains no temporary password value and only reports the pending-handover flag.
Notes: Sensitive-value leak check. Never print the searched credential in a failure message.

Title: Temporary password is not persisted in browser storage or the URL
Preconditions: A user was just created from the UI.
Steps: 1) Read localStorage and sessionStorage for the tenant origin; 2) Read the current URL; 3) Search both for the handover credential
Expected Result: The handover credential is absent from browser storage and from the URL.
Test Data: accepted origin from the run storage state
Notes: playwright/.auth documents admiezo-active-tenant-id in localStorage. Verify no credential is written.

Title: Every provisioning response is traceable to a member, a user and an expiry
Preconditions: One user created by the User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Read id, user_id and expires_at from the handover; 2) Match the catalog member row by id
Expected Result: The handover and the catalog row agree on member id, user id and state, giving one traceable record per create.
Notes: No dedicated audit endpoint is documented. Traceability is asserted through the catalog only.

Title: One handover credential event exists per created member
Preconditions: Three users created in one run by the same User Manager.
Steps: 1) Read the catalog members created in the run; 2) Count pending-handover flags per member; 3) Re-read the catalog twice
Expected Result: Each member carries one consistent handover state and no repeated credential event appears.
Notes: Dedicated audit storage is not documented. Record what the catalog exposes across repeated reads.

Title: Refused escalation attempts leave an auditable trace
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up. One refused university_admin create already performed.
Steps: 1) Repeat a refused university_admin create; 2) Read any documented audit, alert or access-request surface in the catalog
Expected Result: The refusal is visible in an auditor-facing surface, or its absence is raised as a product gap.
Notes: No provisioning audit route exists in api/endpoints/routes.ts. Raise as a product question if nothing records it.

Title: Fifteen users provisioned in one session all appear in the catalog
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up. Active centre exists.
Steps: 1) Create 15 scanner operators with run-unique emails; 2) Read each status code; 3) Re-read the catalog and count the new members
Expected Result: All 15 creates succeed and all 15 members appear exactly once in the catalog.
Notes: Bulk onboarding pressure case. Keep the batch behind DVS_ALLOW_WRITES and clean up after the run.

Title: A newly provisioned user can be found by searching the member list
Preconditions: At least 100 members exist in the tenant and one new user was just created.
Steps: 1) Open User management; 2) Search the member list for the new email; 3) Read the result row
Expected Result: The search returns the new user with the intended role and centre, so operators do not rely on scrolling.
Notes: A search control on the member list was not captured. Confirm the filter exists before automating.

Title: Double-submitting Create user creates one membership
Preconditions: User Manager on the Add university user form with valid data and a completed step-up.
Steps: 1) Click Create user twice in quick succession; 2) Read the resulting members; 3) Count catalog rows for the email
Expected Result: Only one membership is created and the handover is shown once, so a double click cannot duplicate a user.
Notes: Duplicate-submission guard was not captured. If two rows appear, raise a data-integrity defect.

Title: User Manager session ends after the configured inactivity timeout
Preconditions: User Manager signed in. policy.session_timeout_minutes read from the catalog.
Steps: 1) Sign in and leave the workspace idle past session_timeout_minutes; 2) Attempt a protected read; 3) Read the UI
Expected Result: The session ends, the login page is required again and no protected read succeeds with the stale cookie.
Notes: Needs a live wait or an approved policy change. Never shorten the timeout on a shared tenant without approval.

Title: A create interrupted by a reload leaves no partial member
Preconditions: User Manager mid-create with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Submit the create; 2) Reload the page before the response is handled; 3) Re-read the catalog for the email
Expected Result: The member is either fully created with a handover or absent, never present without a usable handover state.
Notes: Partial-write behaviour was not captured. Record the resulting member state.

Title: Retrying a failed create does not duplicate the user
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up. The first attempt is forced to fail by an aborted connection.
Steps: 1) Abort the create request; 2) Retry once with the same payload and the same Idempotency-Key; 3) Count catalog rows for the email
Expected Result: At most one member exists for the email after the retry.
Test Data: single run-unique email, one Idempotency-Key reused
Notes: utils/apiClient.ts sends a fresh Idempotency-Key per write. Confirm whether a retry with the same key is honoured.

Title: Two parallel creates for different users both succeed with distinct ids
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up and two run-unique emails.
Steps: 1) Fire both membership creates in parallel on the same session; 2) Read both status codes and ids
Expected Result: Both creates return 2xx with different member ids and neither response overwrites the other.
Test Data: two run-unique emails, same role and centre
Notes: Distinct from the sequential two-create case: one session, two concurrent requests.

Title: Two parallel creates for the same email yield one member
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up and one run-unique email.
Steps: 1) Fire two identical membership creates in parallel; 2) Read both status codes; 3) Count catalog rows for the email
Expected Result: Exactly one create succeeds, the other fails with a 4xx conflict and only one member row exists.
Test Data: one run-unique email, two parallel requests
Notes: Uniqueness race. A 5xx for the losing request is a defect: the conflict must surface as a validation error.

Title: Concurrent sessions are limited by the policy
Preconditions: User Manager credentials available. policy.maximum_concurrent_sessions read from the catalog.
Steps: 1) Sign in twice with the same account; 2) Read the outcome of the second session; 3) Attempt a protected read from both
Expected Result: The behaviour follows maximum_concurrent_sessions, with either the oldest session ended or the new sign-in refused.
Notes: Session-limit enforcement is not documented. Record which of the two behaviours occurs.

Title: Concurrent step-up and create from two tabs keeps the module list consistent
Preconditions: User Manager signed in on two tabs, both on the Add university user form.
Steps: 1) Step up in tab A; 2) Create user X in tab A and user Y in tab B in parallel; 3) Read both handovers and catalog rows
Expected Result: Both members carry the module list submitted from their own tab, with no cross-contamination.
Test Data: two run-unique emails with different enabled_modules
Notes: Guards against shared form state leaking between tabs. Record the resulting module lists.

Title: Security catalog read stays inside the configured timeout
Preconditions: Populated tenant with at least 100 members. User Manager session.
Steps: 1) Time 10 sequential catalog reads; 2) Compare each with the API timeout used by the framework
Expected Result: Every read completes inside the configured timeout with no error response.
Notes: Assert against the configured timeout, never a hand-written number.

Title: Bulk provisioning of twenty users finishes inside the run timeout
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Create 20 users sequentially; 2) Measure the total duration; 3) Compare with the configured test timeout
Expected Result: All 20 creates complete inside the configured timeout so bulk onboarding stays operable.
Notes: Measure only. A failure here is a throughput defect, not a flaky test.

Title: Catalog read with five hundred members stays responsive
Preconditions: Tenant seeded with about 500 members.
Steps: 1) Time the catalog read three times; 2) Read the response size; 3) Compare with the configured timeout
Expected Result: Reads stay inside the configured timeout and the member list remains renderable.
Notes: Seeding 500 members may need an approved bulk path. Skip the case rather than fake the volume.

Title: Handover creation stays inside the timeout under parallel load
Preconditions: User Manager with a valid step-up.
Steps: 1) Fire 5 parallel creates; 2) Time each response; 3) Compare with the configured timeout
Expected Result: Every create answers inside the configured timeout with no 5xx under parallel load.
Notes: Parallel-load latency was not captured. Record the slowest response.

Title: Step-up dialog exposes labels, traps focus and closes with Escape
Preconditions: Sensitive-action dialog open.

Expected Result: The dialog is announced with an accessible name, focus cannot leave it and Escape dismisses it without creating anything.

Expected Result: The default module list and the centre requirement are shown before submission, so the operator can review least privilege.
Notes: Section 14 step 7 requires reviewing Module access for the role. Confirm it is visible before submit.

Title: Handover sheet stays on screen until Done and states the expiry

Title: Validation errors name the offending field

Expected Result: Each error identifies the offending field and never exposes an internal reason or stack detail.

Expected Result: One append-only row names the User Manager, the target user and the create action.
